items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: She was, you might say, like my boss because she paid my expenses and paid my salary

ctx.x: I went over there. What was her name that owned a record company? She and her husband owned a record company for many years. [Eddie and Nicole Barclay. The name of their company was Barclay Records.] Anyway, she had me come over there. She was, you might say, like my boss because she paid my expenses and paid my salary

over there while I appeared at that club. I can’t think of her name at the moment. She had a record company. She and her husband had a record company. The name escapes me. Anyway, I played. I think I did two or three weeks at this club on the Left Bank that we mentioned with Kenny Clarke in the house band. It was a lot of enjoyment to work with Kenny. He had his own personal style of drumming that was typically, uniquely Kenny Clarke. It was a wonderful style of play. I wrote a head arrangement, you might call…
